subject: Learning Methods
title: Progressive Summarization
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Progressive Summarization.

hook.text: Tiago Forte proposed a layered approach: highlight once, bold the best highlights, then summarize the bold in your own.

buildup.text: Layer 1: raw notes. Layer 2: bold passages. Layer 3: highlights within bold. Layer 4: your own summary.

discovery.text: Each pass extracts the most important content while leaving the full original intact. Nothing is deleted, only surfaced.

twist.text: Not every note needs all four layers. Only invest deeper distillation in notes you actually revisit and use.

climax.text: Let usage drive distillation. Notes you open often get more layers. Notes you never reopen stay at layer one.

punchline.text: Distill only what you use. Let usage guide the effort.

quiz.question: What principle guides how many layers of progressive summarization a note receives?
options: All notes should reach layer four immediately
Only notes that are actually revisited and used deserve deeper layers
Notes from books get more layers than lecture notes
